APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF JUNE 16, 2020

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:05 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Maria Morales, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – absent
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Jerry Velasco, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  WITH THE FOLLOWING EDITS/CHANGES TO THE AGENDA:

  Item 4.1 has been pulled.

  SPECIALLY ADDED AGENDA ITEM:

  4.3  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6 –
  Conference with Labor Negotiator – Unrepresented Employees:

  Unrepresented Employees: All

  City’s Designated Negotiator: Alma K. Martinez, City Manager and John
  Nguyen, Human Resources/Risk Management Director

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Morales  4-0 (Councilmember Ancona absent)

4.  CLOSED SESSION (6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 16, 2020

If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on
Closed Session Items 4.2 and 4.3.

Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at
approximately 6:07 p.m. Councilmember Ancona joined the City Council in
Closed Session for the entirety of Closed Session. Councilmember Martinez
Muela did not participate in Closed Session. Mayor Quintero and the City Council
reconvened from Closed Session at approximately 7:06 pm.

Assistant City Attorney Richard Padilla reported out of Closed Session with
respect to Items 4.2 and 4.3.

4.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2) and
  54956.9(e)(1) – Conference with Legal Counsel to Discuss Facts and
  Circumstances which May Create Exposure to Litigation – One (1) Matter.

  Item has been pulled.

  General update, no final action

  2
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 16, 2020

  4.3  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6 – Conference

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Morales  5-0

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS

  (Commencing at 6:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as the City Council reconvene from Closed
  Session/Short Recess)

5.  INVOCATION:  Mayor Quintero

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  Chief of Police, David Reynoso. Present

7.  RECOGNITIONS, HONORS AND COMMUNITY INTEREST PRESENTATIONS: No
  material submitted.

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions

  3
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 16, 2020

  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
  must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
  religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
  marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

  Gabriel Ramirez – Good Evening El Monte city council, staff, business owners and
  residents of El Monte. During these difficult times with Pandemic and the injustice that is
  happening across the nation. Mayor of Andre Quintero you came out on the city
  YouTube on June 3 talking about expressing peacefully the 1st Amendment Rights and
  protesting peacefully. That contradicts and you have a history of violating public
  speakers who you don't agree with 1st Amendment during public comments. You also
  called "cowards" to protesters who are peacefully protesting outside of the public
  servants house who are protesting for the injustice of police brutality and other issues
  within in the city of El Monte.

9.  CITY TREASURER’S REPORT: No material submitted.

13.  PUBLIC HEARINGS:

  13.1  A Public Hearing to Consider and Approve the First Reading of an Ordinance
  Amending Title 8 (Health and Safety), Chapter 8.10 (Retail Sales of Tobacco
  Products) of the El Monte Municipal Code, to Prohibit the Sale of all Flavored
  Tobacco, Including but Not Limited to E-Cigarettes and Vape Products.

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1.  Open the public hearing;
  2.  Receive presentation from staff;
  3.  Pose question to staff;
  4.  Allow members of the public to offer comment;
  5.  Pose follow-up questions to staff;
  6.  Close the public hearing; and
  7.  Approve the proposed Ordinance by no less than three (3) votes for first
  reading.

  Total Cost: N/A  Account No:  N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  Ordinance No. 2980

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Councilmember Velasco  5-0
  Open P.H.

  Christy Zamani – I would like to thank you for your leadership in exploring a ban on
  flavored tobacco products in the City Of El Monte. In passing this effective safeguard
  you will be joining a number of neighboring cities in protecting youth from a lifetime of
  tobacco use and addiction. This is important. Hopefully, after passing this public health
  victory you can explore further restrictions on smoking/vaping in outdoor public spaces.

  George Johnson – I came to the first two meetings when this item was on the agenda,
  bringing a hookah with me for the visual aid. Hookah for nearly a millennia has been
  used by many cultures and is deeply important in the social fabric of family and business
  meetings. The issue of youth access to vaping products has nothing to do with the
  cultural expression of smoking hookah. We have been swept up in the tidal wave of
  legislation trying to address the youth vaping at astounding rates, yet hookah is not the
  problem. Hookah has the lowest consumption rate of any tobacco on the market.
  Hookah tobacco for nearly 500 years has been preserved in honey and molasses thus
  making it a "flavored product" yes modernt times producers have made modern flavors
  to the product. But hookah by its nature is exclusively a flavored product. So a ban on
  flavored tobacco will be a complete ban on all hookah tobacco. The availability of
  products like mine are being driven to extinction along with many people's livelihoods. I
  fear the repercussions of not taking careful consideration for an "Exemption for
  traditional non-electronic hookahs products" will devastate an already distrusted and
  marginalized community. My grandparents who I live with and care for are Nisei
  Japanese Americans who lost their business and homes in a time of fear. If I lose my

  8
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 16, 2020

business I will not be able to provide for them and do not know how to tell them that.
Please consider carving out Traditional hookah products from this ordinance and leave
them in 21 and older establishments.

Primo Castro – The American Cancer Society Cancer Action Network (ACS CAN) is
committed to protecting the health and well-being of the residents of El Monte through
evidence-based policy and legislative solutions designed to eliminate cancer as a major
health problem. ACS CAN supports efforts to reduce youth tobacco use and eliminating
the sale of flavored tobacco products is an important part of a comprehensive approach
to preventing youth from ever beginning a deadly addiction to tobacco. We support your
efforts in eliminating the sale of all flavored tobacco products, including menthol
cigarettes, within the city of El Monte, and without exemptions through the passage of
this ordinance before you. We strongly encourage this council to adopt this ordinance,
prohibiting the citywide sale of all flavored tobacco products, without exemptions. Taking
this important public health step will help to prevent young people in El Monte from ever
beginning this deadly addiction, as well as help to support those who are trying to quit.

Jivtesh Gill – I am writing to you today on behalf of the American Petroleum and
Convenience Store Association (APCA) representing owners of 1,400 businesses who
are providing jobs, essential services, and products to Californians. Each day, 165
million people visit their favorite neighborhood market resulting in sales that allow the
average convenience store to collect $1.28 million in property, payroll, and sales taxes
for local, state, and federal governments every year. Here in Pleasanton, our association
members are investing in the community by supporting local charities, youth sports
teams, and food drives. The sale of tobacco and e-cigarettes products is a critical part of
our retailers’ business model. Tobacco and e-cigarettes sales drive ancillary sales of
gas, food, and other products and keep us in business. If we lose the ability to sell
tobacco and e-cigarettes products as the city proposes, our customers will go
elsewhere. We oppose this sales ban as it eliminates an entire category of products from
our shelves that adults in this country have the right to buy and enjoy.

Issa Abuaita – I oppose a ban on flavored tobacco without an exemption for Hookah.
Many cultures use hookah like Americans use beer at a barbeque because drinking
alcohol is against their religion. Hookah is completely different than an e-cigarette. First,
it’s used in a large water pipe and difficult to hide, in a backpack for instance. It’s difficult
to use without someone noticing. It takes time to set up. Setting one up actually takes 20
minutes and at least an hour to consume. Because of this, hookah is not very appealing
to youth. Of course, we don’t want our youth to use any tobacco products nor do we
want them using marijuana or alcohol for that matter. Banning hookah just doesn’t raise
the same youth use issues. Specifically, the latest information from the CDC on youth
use of hookah is only 2.6% compared to almost 26 percent for vaping. Please protect
our youth but also save our tax paying businesses, the employees of those business and
the important cultural tradition of hookah by exempting hookah from the flavor ban.

Shaina Vo – I hope all is well and your being safe. I would like to share my story. A
few years ago I use to smoke cigarettes and the carcinogens have effected my
health indeed. But quitting cigarettes is very difficult especially if you live with
someone that also smokes. Since I have converted over to vaping, I notice I feel less
haggard and the smell doesn't remain on my clothing or fingers, and while smoking
outside, the flavored smoke itself doesn't linger like the strong odor of cigarettes. The
tobacco Vape liquids I would purchase are at legitimate stores that have alway oblige

  9
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 16, 2020

by the state rules. No one allowed under 21, strictly. This type of tobacco minus the
carcinogens has helped a lot people I know to quit smoking cigarettes and improve
their health. Why allow the selling of cigarettes but not the vape juice? I ask that the
city please reconsider.

Amanda Staples – In the midst of a time where public health is of utmost concern, we
write in full support of an ordinance to end the sale of flavored tobacco products
including menthol cigarettes in the City of El Monte. There is no price for health and
ending the sale of flavored tobacco will reduce access to the products that are the
tobacco industry’s key strategy for targeting and addicting new smokers, particularly
youth. The American Heart Association is committed to being a relentless force for a
world of longer, healthier lives. Exemptions will weaken the ordinance, creating
loopholes for young people to access flavored tobacco products that lure them into using
addictive, nicotine products. Flavored tobacco products contain nicotine, which can have
a long-term damaging impact on the developing, adolescent brain. The City of El Monte
has the opportunity in this important moment to be a positive force in protecting our
public health, and the American Heart Association respectfully asks for your support of
this vital policy to ensure that all El Monte residents have longer, healthier lives

Arabi Hassan – BREATHE CA of Los Angeles County strongly urges you to pass a full
flavor ban in the City of El Monte, including all flavored tobacco products such as
menthol, spearmint, and mint products.

Annie Tegen – The Campaign for Tobacco-Free Kids would like thank El Monte City
Council for their strong leadership last week on this life-saving ordinance. I’d like to
thank you for standing up for kids, and fighting back against the decades of targeting by
the tobacco industry. We strongly support the ordinance to end the sale of flavored
tobacco products in all retailers, including menthol cigarettes and all flavored cigars. This
is a critical step that will help protect children living in El Monte from the unrelenting
efforts by the tobacco industry to hook them to a deadly addiction. The flavors lure kids
in, and the nicotine hooks them. Flavored tobacco products are designed to alter the
taste and reduce the harshness of tobacco products so they are more appealing and
easy for beginners, who are almost always kids. These products are pervasive and are
marketed and sold in a variety of kid-friendly flavors. With their colorful packaging and
sweet flavors, flavored tobacco products are often hard to distinguish from the candy
displays near which they are frequently placed in retail outlets and often at eye level for
kids. We hope that tonight, El Monte will join over 55 other California cities and counties,
and pass a comprehensive ordinance to end the sale of all flavored tobacco products
without exemptions. This ordinance will reduce health inequities and save lives.

Jaime Rojas – Please find attached a letter from the National Association of Tobacco
Outlets opposing agenda item #13.1 as written. Also attached is also the FDA's annual
retailer compliance checks from 2012-2019. In those 7 years, El Monte retailers have a
near perfect 99% compliance check passing rate. In fact, the only violations in those
compliance checks did not concern minors, but was a packaging issue. Based on the
California Healthy Kids Survey of 9th and 11th graders in the El Monte Union High
School District, use of tobacco products are at historic lows and in two categories almost
zero: 85% had never smoked a cigarette, only 4% said they had smoked any cigarettes
in the past 30 days, and none reported smoking regularly; 97% had never used
smokeless tobacco, only 1% reported having used any smokeless tobacco products in
the previous 30 days and none reported using smokeless tobacco regularly; only 2% of

  10
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 16, 2020

these students reported using e-cigarette products regularly; Cigar and pipe tobacco are
not even surveyed, suggesting their usage is even less. We urge the El Monte City
Council not to move forward with any attempt to impose a ban on all flavored tobacco
products, and to certainly not even consider making any such changes under the
existing state of emergency we find ourselves.

Alisha Lopez – Good Evening Honorable Mayor Quintero, Mayor Pro-Tem Morales, and
Council Members, my name is Alisha Lopez and I am here tonight on behalf of Day One,
a local non-profit organization. I am also here tonight to speak on behalf of the Love
Your Lungs Coalition, a coalition of El Monte residents and public health experts who
believe you have the right to breathe clean air in smokefree spaces. Day One and the
Love Your Lungs Coalition support tobacco control and prevention policies that seek to
protect youth from dangerous and appealing products, such as flavored tobacco. Not
only can these products be regulated at the point of sale, but they can also be regulated
by prohibiting the use in outdoor areas and reducing the social modeling for youth in the
community. We applaud your leadership for addressing the problem of youth’s easy
access to harmful and addictive tobacco flavored products through the ordinance being
discussed tonight, and look forward to an open conversation about how prohibitions on
smoking/vaping in outdoor areas can be addressed further.

Veer Partners – I am the owner of the ARCO gas station on Santa Anita Ave. I have had
the pleasure of speaking and meeting most of you all and I hope you are all staying safe
and healthy during this unusual time in all of our lives. I understand tonight is a call in
hearing and one of the topics addressed will be the proposition of a flavored tobacco
ban. Ever since our inception as a business owner in this city we have been pleased and
grateful in working with your staff and personnel and truly attribute the city's way of doing
things to our business success. With the help of the city and the community we have
become one of the city's top 25 sales tax generators, and we are pleased to be making a
positive impact in our community.

Emilio Silva – I am a resident of El Monte. I was born and raised here, went to school
here and currently work here. I love my city and I want to be able to support the
businesses here. I think it’s unfair that we need to go to surrounding cities to buy our
vape products. I want the money I make and spend to go back into making our city
better. I would much rather smoke vape than smoke cigarettes and potentially burn
something down. If it does end up getting banned, it will just eventually get unbanned
and we’re going to have to do this all over. Just follow the state and federal regulations
or tax us more if you have to. We can use those extra taxes to help the city out or use
those for resources for homeless and those in need. Don’t make us responsible vape
users scape goats for the kids who died from using fake THC cartridges, not vape
products.

Leo – I am fully against this vape ban in El Monte, I thought it was a nationwide but I
found out it was just for the City which I found concerning. My go to vape shop warned
me about it so I had to definitely say something.

Mynor Ramos – My name is Mynor Ramos and I represent Jungle Vape N' Smoke. A
local El Monte business located at 2800 Peck Road, Unit A, El Monte, CA 91733. One of
our specialties is selling vape products in different flavors. As a business in this, now,
controversial issue, we understand the risks associated with these products. However, I
consider we have to look at this issue from different perspectives. Banning vaping is not

  11
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 16, 2020

a wise move, it has more cons than pros from every angle we look at it. Please consider
these facts and we hope you can make the right decision.

Jisela Fredman – Volunteers of America – In favor of the ban on flavored tobacco.

Dr. Wein – In favor of the ban on flavored tobacco.

Jeannette Rodriguez - In favor of the ban on flavored tobacco.

Geo Galarza – Against a ban on flavored tobacco.

Jaime Rojas – Against a ban on flavored tobacco.
